Built read-only from design/handoff-v46/ (frozen v46), the 00-project-context stakeholder/PM records, the 07.2 / 07.3 stakeholder correction records, inventory v3 and register v2. Board text quoted from the v46 boards; derived/ files used only as a search aid. Status legend: CONFIRMED-STAKEHOLDER = in a stakeholder/PM-confirmed record or an owner binding constraint; CONFIRMED-DESIGN = approved on v46 boards / LD-x / M-x / C-x but not in a stakeholder record; PROVISIONAL = designed safe treatment pending decision; UNRESOLVED = open with no safe treatment for the connected build.
authorityOrder: handoff JSON (index; board wins — differences reported)
Stakeholder-confirmed records govern business behaviour (STK31 > 07.2/07.3 for later points > PM-16…18 > PM-01…12)

verification.openDecisionsJsonVsB808: All 79 batch decisions and 35 register-T items in open-decisions.json match the B8-08 board tables cell-for-cell (0 mismatches, 114 IDs).
verification.registerTMissingIds: T-27 (decided LD-3) and T-37 (decided C-3) are not in registerT by design.

businessRules.rule: PUBLIC is a surface, not an authenticated role. There are exactly seven authenticated roles: Student, Faculty, Institute Admin, Vendor, Academic Reviewer, Content Manager, Super Admin.

No eighth role. Student and Learner are one role; Institute Admin and Tenant Admin are one role; internal BITS/WILP content teams work through the Vendor role. Do not create Internal Content Developer, Employee or similar roles.
One product, one shell, one router; a sidebar item exists only when its screen exists — no disabled placeholders, no 'static' items.

Role guards per workspace: an address belonging to another workspace shows XS-06 'This page isn’t part of your workspace' ('You’re signed in to the Student workspace. This address belongs to a different workspace.' · Back to Home · Help). Never show route names, role codes, status codes or technical causes.

Actions are offered only where the design offers them (e.g. no Publish for the Super Admin, approve-only device transfers). No permission matrix was designed; permissions are derived from boards + entities owner/writer + flows actor, and doubtful cases go to the owner.
No role switcher, 'Viewing as…', sample-account chooser or 'choose a workspace' step in product UI (XS-02 multi-role DEFER). A developer account switcher, if any, lives outside the product chrome.
No cross-role links: a role's frame never links into another role's workspace. Cross-role movement only through shared public pages (request status) and the shared Help & support family.

Sign in offers 'Sign in with your institution (SSO)' and 'Sign in with e-mail'; each person lands on their role's home; session expiry returns them to the page they were on. Forgot password / activation (XS-04) only says 'contact your institution administrator'. Provider and password policy are open.
businessRules.notes: SSO + platform-authentication fallback is stakeholder-confirmed (STK31-44); the concrete behaviour is a provisional mock (real auth out of scope).

businessRules.rule: Shell banner states (XS-08): 'Your institution’s access is paused — your work is kept' and 'Your account is inactive'.

Help & support (XS-07) is one template in the same place in all seven workspaces (sidebar bottom and account menu): Report a problem (what happened, where — pre-filled, optional screenshot; nothing else) + My reports + report detail; reference SUP-nnnn. No response times or SLA promises.

Support reports are resolved in Super Admin › Operations › Support: Open · Resolved · Reopened. Resolve needs a note shown to the reporter; Reopen is a plain confirmation. No response-time target (ND-14).
Hierarchy is Programme / Course / Experiment / Technology format. There is no mandatory Module layer anywhere.

Programme is held on the Student record only (B2-06/B2-07) and is not a navigation level. Engineering area is a catalogue grouping of courses set in Academic structure (B7-07); Course → Experiment → format is the navigable chain.
businessRules.notes: Owner binding constraint. Differs from the stakeholder's 'Programme / Department / Academic Stream' grouping level (STK31-12) — see conflicts.

businessRules.rule: Formats are WEB · AR · VR · MR (MR retained). Technology is a selectable dimension of an Experiment, not a separate product.
Experiment is the publication unit: one catalogue entry per Experiment with only the formats that passed governance; never four catalogue products; unpublished experiments never appear.
Learning outcomes: one set per Experiment, common to all formats, authored by the Academic Reviewer; Vendor sees them read-only; Faculty/Student/public read-only.
businessRules.notes: Ownership is stakeholder-confirmed (STK31-08); 'one set per Experiment' is LD-3.

businessRules.rule: Every Experiment maps to a Course; the Vendor picks only from courses assigned to them; the course list comes from Academic structure and Platform roles.
businessRules.notes: Who performs the mapping (PQ-20) remains open; v46 safe treatment: Vendor selects from assigned courses.

businessRules.rule: Academic structure belongs to the Super Admin: Add area · Add course · Rename · Edit description · Move a course to another area. Names must be unique; renaming warns where the name shows. No Retire, no area artwork upload. Moving a course is blocked while students or Faculty are filed against it; published experiments, institutions' access and Vendor course lists move with it and are listed before the move.
The platform is the sole definer of the canonical catalogue and academic structure; an Institute Admin cannot redefine it or assign content outside the institution's approved set.

Two course codes, two owners: the platform course code (e.g. ME ZG523) is edited only by the Content Manager (M-2) and shown read-only to the Super Admin in Academic structure; the institution's own course code + optional semester belongs to the Institute Admin. Platform code ≠ institution code; blank platform code allowed.
businessRules.notes: Conflicts with stakeholder 07.2-E ('Super Admin will also get access to it') — see conflicts.

businessRules.rule: Semester is optional everywhere; the only course-code validation designed is 'a semester needs a code'; no code format is invented.
Course code shown: Students see the institution code (the BITS code until one exists); public pages show the platform code (blank allowed).
Whether a new, empty engineering area shows in the public explorer is undecided; adding an area changes nothing public in the designed screens.
Published, institution access, Student entitlement, runtime activity and learning completion are five different states. Never derive one from another.
Publishing or releasing never grants institution or Student access. Publish dialog: 'it gives no one access'; Release: 'Release grants or changes no institution’s access'.
Institution access (ACC access plan) ≠ Student access (SACC grant): Content access and Student access are separate destinations; Give students access is its own guided flow.

Available technology ≠ entitlement: chips say 'Available in'; the Student sees 'Not included for your institution' (format not in the plan) vs 'Not available for this experiment' (format not published).

A Student sees only experiments given to them; an experiment the institution holds but has not given never appears; opening its address shows ST-19 'This experiment isn’t available to you'. Course rows say what was given ('1 experiment given to you · WEB and VR available'), never a progress verdict.
sources: design/handoff-v46/canvas-v46/project/B2-11-My-Courses.dc.html 'Only what was given', 'Course rows: access only'

businessRules.rule: The public catalogue shows only published experiments; a new experiment appears only after the Content Manager's publication decision.

B2B selection is a selection basket + request preparation, not a checkout: it lives in the visitor's browser session until the request is sent, needs no account, and is never called cart, basket, checkout or buy; no prices.

The request form asks only institution and contact details (+ selection, licences, term); it never asks internal/external, payment details or prices. Requester identity, return path and account creation are open (T-01 / R01): no OTP, magic link or registration.
The request reference (REQ-0042) identifies the request but is never a key to its details; the status page shows private details and how a requester is identified before seeing it is open.
Access is never granted before Super Admin approval; the Super Admin is the in-product approver of institutional requests.

Super Admin request decisions: Approve request · Approve a smaller scope (a real difference + reason recorded) · Request more information (reason). There is no Decline control and no Declined state or filter (T-02).
businessRules.notes: Decline itself is WAIT FOR DECISION (T-02 / R21).

businessRules.rule: Internal / external is set by the Super Admin at the first approval of a new institution and is required to complete approval; the requester never chooses it; later requests show the route set at first approval.
businessRules.notes: That both routes exist is stakeholder-confirmed (STK31-19); the classification rule ND-07 is open.

businessRules.rule: Four separate events: (1) institution record created at the first approval of a new institution — a record is not access; (2) request approval; (3) payment confirmation — external only, not on the decision page; (4) institutional access activation — internal on approval, external only after payment is confirmed. Activation creates the access plan the Institute Admin sees. 'Approved' never reads as 'active'; 'Payment started' never reads as 'paid'.

Payment (external only) is provider-neutral: summary of what will be activated, no amount until pricing exists, no payment method collected, no refund wording, no manual 'mark paid' (R06); only success activates; failure → 'Payment not confirmed' + Try payment again.
'Request more information' keeps the request open with the reason shown to the requester; there is no reply form (PU-11 not designed).
Requests from a paused institution can't be decided until the pause ends.
Access term options are Monthly · Quarterly · Yearly; licence quantity comes from the request — there is no universal seat cap; never restore arbitrary sample caps.

Licence figures are shown as the service provides them (e.g. 'Licences 1,284 of 1,650'); copy never explains what an assignment, withdrawal or deactivation does to the count. What consumes a licence (D7) is open.
sources: design/handoff-v46/canvas-v46/project/10-Dialogs.dc.html (withdraw note: 'Licence effects are not described — that rule is open (T-06)')

businessRules.rule: The licence-counting rule itself (what consumes / releases a licence, cross-experiment counting, effect of withdrawal and deactivation) is undecided; boards nevertheless show a 'Waiting for a licence' grant status (e.g. Arun on B3-10), so the mock must return it as a seeded/provided state, never compute it.
sources: design/handoff-v46/canvas-v46/project/B8-03-Terminology-and-Visual-Consistency.dc.html status vocabulary 'Waiting for a licence' (15 uses)

businessRules.rule: Renewal mirrors the current plan; 'More licences' asks the number only (no term); new experiments/formats are requested through the public catalogue; both create a REQ decided in Super Admin › Requests; approval leads to the payment page and nothing changes until payment is confirmed. Renewal follows the same payment route as initial onboarding (internal: no payment).
businessRules.notes: Route rule is stakeholder-confirmed (07.2-D); whether a renewal/expansion may change licences, formats or term (D26 / D27) is provisional.

businessRules.rule: Only the Institute Admin raises requests to BITS (renewal / more licences); other roles are not shown doing so.
No direct institution creation (institutions come only from approved requests — T-09) and no access-plan amendment (changes come through a new request — T-08).
businessRules.notes: Stakeholder STK31-21/24 give the SA tenant creation and allocation authority — see conflicts.

businessRules.rule: Institution status handling by the Super Admin: Pause (from active or ending soon) · Restore (from paused), each DL-2 with a reason kept in the history. Awaiting-payment and ended institutions have no status action; an ended plan returns only through a renewal request. Pausing is reversible and keeps everyone's work.

While an institution is paused: its Institute Admin, Faculty and Students see the paused banner; Students can't open experiments; pages are read-only until BITS lifts the pause; the Institute Admin has no 'Give students access'; the access plan and all work are kept. Faculty get the shared banner only (OD-B7-07).

Assign Institute Admin (SA): name + work e-mail, validated; offered once access is active (awaiting-payment institutions say so instead); nothing is sent — how they first sign in is open (T-11). Without an Institute Admin nobody can give students access.
businessRules.notes: That the SA assigns the Institute Admin is stakeholder-confirmed; timing and invitation are provisional.

businessRules.rule: 15-day expiry: access ending within 15 days shows 'Ending soon' / 'Reminder due' as a status only — nothing is sent from the product (T-31).
businessRules.notes: For the frontend build only.

businessRules.rule: The 15-day expiry reminder to the tenant is a REQUIRED platform capability; an in-product attention state does not discharge it; the channel must not be invented (ND-16).
businessRules.notes: No safe treatment in v46 satisfies the requirement (v46 sends nothing). Production/backend blocker; not a frontend blocker. See conflicts.

businessRules.rule: Experiment is the Student-access unit (LD-1): the Institute Admin selects experiments inside a course of an active access plan; formats are shown read-only as 'Available to your institution' and inherited; there is no WEB / AR / VR / MR picker anywhere in the flow.
Published experiments of the course that are not in the access plan are listed 'Not in your access plan' and cannot be ticked.

Grants go to a Student individually or to a group through the same Give students access flow (no separate group engine); the confirmation names each grant ('Rahul Verma → Shell-and-Tube Heat Exchanger → SACC-0310 → Active'); Student access lists one row per student × experiment with how it was given and its status in words — no anonymous allocation counts.

Withdraw applies to individual grants only: DL-2 with a required reason; work is kept; the grant stays in history ('Show withdrawn'); group grants are changed on the group; the dialog says nothing about licences.

Overlapping grants: each grant is shown with its own state; withdrawing names only the grant it ends and says the other is not changed; no screen states whether the student can still open the experiment through the other grant.

Whether a Student can still open an experiment through a group grant after the individual grant is withdrawn (OD-B2-01), whether a late group member receives the group's experiments (OD-B2-02), and what removing a member does to group-given access (B2-08) are undecided and the Student-side outcome is not drawn — the shared store has no designed answer.
Inactive students can't open experiments while inactive (group grants are shown for the members the group has when access is given).
Remove a member from a group: DL-1 confirm; they leave the group, their record stays; nothing else is stated.
Add student (single form): Full name (required), Institution e-mail (required, unique), Student ID (required, unique), Programme (optional), Group (optional).

Student CSV import: one row per student; columns student_id, full_name, email, programme, course, course_code — all required; duplicate IDs inside the file or IDs/e-mails already in People are errors with the row number; no warning conditions; errors block the import (all-or-nothing interim, T-24); template download has exactly these columns; no XLSX, no ERP precedence.
sources: design/handoff-v46/canvas-v46/project/B2-07-Add-and-Import.dc.html 'Required columns', 'Duplicates', 'Warnings', 'Commit mode — interim, not final', 'Not designed'
businessRules.notes: Stakeholder STK31-26 also lists Semester (optional), Organisation (optional) and Plan Terms ('if possible') — not in v46; see conflicts.

businessRules.rule: Adding a person creates a record only: no invitation, activation or provisioning UI; 'Contact your institution administrator'.

The Institute Admin may deactivate and reactivate a student account ('Deactivate account…', 'Reactivate account'); the Super Admin may also change a student's status as an override with a required reason ('An override — kept in the history. The Institute Admin normally changes this.').

Faculty courses: the Institute Admin assigns Faculty to courses; removing the last Faculty member of a course with written answers waiting warns before confirming; when a course has no Faculty its written answers can't be marked and the Institute Admin is warned on the Overview.
Faculty scope is only the courses the Institute Admin assigned and, inside them, only experiments the institution holds.

Usage (Institute Admin only here): per experiment × format counts — students with access, started, completed, sessions; no charts, licence usage or 'in use' figures, percentages, exports or Reports page; feedback is never shown.

Progress is per technology format: Not started · In progress (last saved) · Completed (date, from the system). No percentage, no aggregate or experiment-/course-level completion verdict, and resources never count as progress.

'Completed' is set by the system only — an event reported by the simulation. The Student cannot mark it and it is never inferred from a launch ('The simulation reports that you finished. You can’t mark it yourself.').
businessRules.notes: The exact event contract (T-12 / A-06 / D25) is open; the safe treatment is complete.

businessRules.rule: Resources open in a new tab; opening marks 'Opened' and nothing else; states not opened · opening · opened (date) · couldn’t open + try again · none attached · loading · list failed · paused.
No locks or required order: suggested order Resources → Simulation → Assessment → Progress, with one primary action.
businessRules.notes: PM-09 retained gating (D-07, D-20) — see conflicts.

businessRules.rule: A Student can use only the formats given to them (inherited from the plan); AR/VR/MR pages give information-only setup steps and never promise a store, download or MDM route.

Feedback: one record per Student × Experiment × format, offered ('Give feedback on WEB') only after that format is Completed; five 1–5 ratings + optional Additional comments; submitted once, no edit or resubmit; 'Feedback sent · WEB · <date>'.
Feedback is never shown to staff: no staff feedback views or analytics anywhere; Usage has no feedback column; neutral copy.

Device transfer is authorisation of a different device, not shipping. Chain: Student requests (New device required + optional note) → Institute Admin forwards ('Forward to BITS', DL-1; cannot approve or decline) → Super Admin approves (approve only, DL-1). No Decline: a request BITS doesn't approve stays 'Forwarded'. One open request at a time (assumption). No device registry.
businessRules.notes: The Student → Institute Admin → Super Admin chain is stakeholder-confirmed (07.2-C, superseding STK31-38's Student → SA routing); approve-only and the field set are provisional.

businessRules.rule: A device request can't be forwarded when the institution is paused or has no Institute Admin; the Student sees 'can’t be forwarded yet' with Help.
Faculty own assessment creation, configuration and marking; a Student never configures an assessment; Faculty is the only human evaluator of written answers.

Pass mark and rules belong to each assessment; there are no platform defaults: a new assessment starts with every field empty and no option selected; sample values (50%, 2 attempts, 14 Nov 2026 23:59) are never defaults.
One assessment per experiment per institution (prototype rule): a second is refused at step 1 with a link to the existing assessment, labelled open.

An assessment is Ready when it has a name and introduction, its rules and at least one question; students who have the experiment can then see and start it. There is no 'Make available' or close control; the deadline is shown as a date only and nothing claims late attempts are blocked or allowed.
When students see results: Immediately after marking · After the deadline · On a date (+ release date); no option pre-selected; results and answers released together.
businessRules.notes: The Faculty-controlled option set is stakeholder-confirmed (STK31-32); BITS/Taxila default (ND-10) pending.

businessRules.rule: Question types: multiple choice (one correct, up to four options) · true or false · written answer with free-text marking guidance. No other types, no timer, no rubric builder.
businessRules.notes: Three types are stakeholder-confirmed (STK31-30); 'no timer' is provisional — PM-08 conflict.

businessRules.rule: Marks are set on the question in the bank and shown per question everywhere.
Question bank Delete: label 'Delete' is settled; DL-1 says the question leaves the bank, its history is kept and assessments that use it keep their copy (mechanism ND-15).

Versioning: editing a used question saves a new version and an assessment changes only when Faculty choose 'Use updated version'; changing an assessment rule after submissions makes a new version — earlier submissions keep theirs; changing when results are shown is warned separately.

Draft with assistance: from the experiment's lab brief or pasted text; 3 or 5 drafts; every draft tagged 'Draft — needs your review' and 'Drafted with assistance'; nothing enters the bank until Faculty add it; discarded drafts leave no trace; no provider named; no suggested marks.
businessRules.notes: Mandatory Faculty review is stakeholder-confirmed (STK31-33); sources differ — see conflicts.

businessRules.rule: Question import: ten-column CSV template; all-or-nothing while any row has an error (interim); missing explanation is a warning.

Attempt: every answer saves as it changes (failed save → Try again; nothing saved is lost); leaving keeps answers and 'Continue attempt' resumes the same attempt; Submit is never automatic, opens DL-1 'You can’t change your answers after submitting' and names unanswered questions; no countdown, no score, no marking guidance shown.
Marking guidance is Faculty-only — never shown to students during the attempt.
Marking a written answer: the mark is required (0 to the question's marks), Faculty feedback optional; queue oldest first; confirmed marks are read-only — no re-marking; no assistant-suggested marks.

Before release a Student sees no figure of any kind (no score, pass/not passed or correct answers) — only 'Submitted — waiting for marking' or 'Result not released yet'. After release: headline (You passed / Not passed this time) → score card (marks, pass mark as configured, attempt used, release date) → answers with correct answer + explanation.
'Try again' is shown only when not passed and an attempt is left.
Faculty follow-up: 'Inactive for N days' filter (7 / 14 / 30; activity = opening a format or the assessment — sample); contacting students happens outside the platform; no messaging or reminders.
Faculty Export CSV exports the list on screen, including whether each result is released to the student; no reports page.
Faculty never see Student feedback and see no score before marking; progress per format in words with completion date.

First publication: Vendor → Academic Reviewer → Content Manager → Published. The Content Manager is the sole first publisher; the Super Admin never publishes first; the Vendor never publishes; Academic Reviewer approval ≠ publication.

Vendor may create an experiment, save and edit a draft, submit for academic review, receive a return, revise and resubmit, and see submission/version history. The Vendor does not propose updates to published content and cannot add a format (VE-10…12, VE-14 not designed).

Submit: a checklist (course & description · formats & delivery · preview & documents — optional) lists missing items with links and sends nothing; DL-1 'This sends it to the Academic Reviewer. It does not publish anything.'; read-only for the Vendor while under review.

Format delivery: WEB = web link + browser and computer needed; AR / VR / MR = app package (label, reference or file, device needed, install notes); optional notes per format; no source code; package fields provisional; delivery mechanism open.
businessRules.notes: Package-vs-link and 'no source code' are stakeholder-confirmed (STK31-37).

businessRules.rule: Catalogue fields (prototype set): course, name, one-sentence summary, description, version; experiment name unique case-insensitively against the catalogue and the Vendor's own experiments; submission ID given on first save; a preview label without a valid link is an error.

When a course is no longer assigned to the Vendor: an unsaved new experiment shows 'no longer one of your assigned courses — choose one of your courses'; a saved experiment in that course opens read-only.

After a resubmit the Vendor sees only 'Submitted — your changes have been submitted for review.'; copy never promises which gate comes next (M-3); DL-1 'Your changes are submitted for review. This does not publish anything.'
A return shows by whom, when, the reason in their words and 'What it refers to' (step · format · field) above the editor, with links to the field.

Academic Reviewer 'Approve' (DL-1): 'Sends it to the Content Manager. Approving does not publish.' — needs at least one learning outcome. 'Return to vendor' (DL-2): reason required; 'What it refers to' optional. No partial approve or per-format decision, no checklist/rubric, no device testing.

Reviewer course scoping: a reviewer sees submissions for the courses in their scope (sample 'You review: ME ZG523 · MEL ZG512 · CHE ZG513'); scopes are assigned in Super Admin › Platform roles; a submission whose course has no reviewer in scope gets stuck.
Outcome edits travel with the reviewer's Approve or Return; edits in progress stay with the reviewer.
Publication check re-reads only: Academic Reviewer approval, learning outcomes, catalogue details, delivery details for each format.

Content Manager 'Publish' (DL-1): appears in the public catalogue under its course with its formats and gives no one access → Published. 'Send back' (DL-2): choose the Academic Reviewer (a re-check) or the Vendor (revise & resubmit) — destination and reason both required; references optional and only for the Vendor. No partial publish, format hold-back, access, licence or Faculty control.
businessRules.notes: Two send-back destinations are stakeholder-confirmed (07.3 R15).

businessRules.rule: Corrections to published content: Content Manager → Academic Reviewer → Super Admin Release / Hold — always (no technical-only shortcut). 'Publish' never appears on this path.

Every change to a published experiment — including 'Edit catalogue details' and 'Edit delivery link' — opens or joins the one correction draft pre-filled with live fields; the live experiment is unchanged until the Super Admin releases it; no review-bypassing 'safe edit'. Three entries, one draft; one open update per experiment; while the update is with the Academic Reviewer or the Super Admin only 'Open update' is offered.
sources: design/handoff-v46/canvas-v46/project/B6-08-Published-and-Correction-Entry.dc.html 'Three entries, one draft', 'An update is in progress', 'Not designed'
businessRules.notes: Conflicts with stakeholder 07.3 R16 (direct CM link edit) — see conflicts.

businessRules.rule: 'Send for academic review' (DL-1) needs a reason, a new version label different from the live version, and at least one change.
A correction may change catalogue details (name, summary, description) and delivery (web link, VR package reference); no format changes; learning outcomes are not in the correction draft.
Withdraw update (DL-2, reason required) is offered while the update is a draft, returned or in academic review — not after approval.

Academic Reviewer 'Approve update' (DL-1): 'It goes to the Super Admin, who decides when to release it. Version 1.2 stays live until then.' → Awaiting release decision; never changes the live experiment. 'Return to the Content Manager' (DL-2): reason only (references on update returns open).

Super Admin 'Release' (DL-1): the new version replaces the live one for everyone (public catalogue and every institution); history keeps every version and decision. 'Hold' asks for a reason the Content Manager sees; the live version stays. 'Lift hold' (DL-1) returns the update to 'Waiting for your decision' and never releases. Release is not offered straight from On hold. The Super Admin never edits the correction.
businessRules.notes: Release/Hold ownership is stakeholder-confirmed (STK31-07); hold mechanics are provisional.

businessRules.rule: What else a Hold affects and whether a held update blocks later corrections are undecided; screens say it is open.
businessRules.notes: Implied behaviour: B6-08 offers only 'Open update' while an update is with the Super Admin, so the mock would block a second correction during a hold — confirm with the owner.

businessRules.rule: The public experiment page and learner frame show 'Version 1.2 / 1.3' so Release can be seen; whether the version is public is open.

Published content is read-only for the Super Admin (no edit, no catalogue form). 'Move status (override)' exists only for a stuck, non-published record: DL-2 with a reason, recorded with the Super Admin's name, never into or out of Published; the one supported move is back to the vendor (record stuck with the Academic Reviewer).
businessRules.notes: Narrower than stakeholder 07.2-F / 07.3 R17 — see conflicts.

businessRules.rule: The Content Manager sees Released / On hold as end states of an update on CM-08.
Changing a platform course code of a course with published experiments is saved directly by the Content Manager (no review step); effects on links or institution codes are not designed.
businessRules.notes: Safe treatment covers the save; downstream effects have no design.

businessRules.rule: Super Admin governs Vendor, Academic Reviewer and Content Manager role holders: register a Vendor / Reviewer; assign scope (all · course · experiment; multiple people per experiment allowed); withdraw a scope (DL-2, reason kept with the scope); restore puts the same scope back in one click with a confirmation and no reason; role holders without scope are flagged. No invitation e-mail, no SSO set-up, no identity-origin rule.
businessRules.notes: Course/experiment-specific assignment is stakeholder-confirmed (STK31-41); restore-without-reason and registration mechanics are provisional.

businessRules.rule: Dialogs: DL-1 Confirm (short confirmation), DL-2 Confirm with reason (return, send back, withdraw, pause, hold and similar — reason required and shown to the person affected; the dialog says who will see it), DL-3 Small edit. Anything longer is a page.

Dialog behaviour: Cancel first (quiet), confirming action last and strongest; destructive confirmations use the red button with initial focus on Cancel; focus moves in, Tab cycles inside, Esc cancels with nothing changed, focus returns to the trigger, a success notice confirms; at 375 px dialogs sit at the bottom full-width with stacked buttons and never more than one field below 600 px.

Validation exactly as drawn: field errors plus an error summary (role alert, linked to fields; summary links move focus to the field); fields keep what was typed; required reasons where shown; duplicate checks where shown (codes, names, scopes).

Status always in words (colour supports, never carries meaning); one state grammar: loading · empty (with next step) · error + retry ('Nothing was lost') · refused with a reason · read-only (saying who has it now) · paused / inactive banner · not available.
No notifications, messages or reminders are sent from the product; statuses are read where the person is.
No report pages and no Reports destination; exports of existing lists only; no KPI dashboards, revenue or fake financial analytics.
Prefer reversible status change over deletion; history is preserved (withdrawn grants, paused institutions, withdrawn scopes, deleted questions keep history).

Public experiment page: hero (title, course, summary, Available in, illustration) → learning outcomes → formats and device needs → preview; one 'Get this for your institution' panel (choose published formats → Add to selection); never prices or 'Buy'; Student access never implied; no 'Reviewed' seal, governance line or academic-quality claim.

'Your institution already has this' and 'Request additional licences' on public pages need a recognised institution and are not designed; 'already has this' appears only inside the Institute Admin workspace.
Out of scope unless separately authorised: real authentication, payment processing, XR runtimes, grading automation and backend persistence. Build typed mock services that return the sample world.
'Composite Wall Conduction' (published, WEB + AR) and 'Conduction Through a Composite Wall' (SUB-0077) stay two separate records while OD-B5-09 is open — no merge, no duplicate-content rule.

The BITS Pilani / WILP logo is an unapproved, labelled placeholder ('BITS Pilani / WILP logo — placeholder'); Public Sans is a working font only and never labelled official; artwork labelled concept artwork, never presented as a simulation capture.

B1-10 (Super Admin Requests) below 760 px: the visually hidden table header's 'Received' sort button must not be focusable while invisible — show the sort as a visible control above the labelled rows (or remove the hidden header's controls from the tab order and provide a visible equivalent).

One connected application state for every shared record (REQ, INST, ACC, SACC, PER, RUN, FB, ASMT/ATT, DTR, SUB, EXP, UPD, AREA/CRS, ROLE, SUP …): a decision in one role's screen is what every other role sees. Board state is per board on the canvas; the product must not be.
